findings.passage: Over the past several weeks, the House has once again turned its attention to the SAVE America Act, legislation that would require documentary proof of citizenship when registering to vote in federal elections. Supporters say it’s necessary to protect election integrity. Critics argue it could make voter registration more difficult for eligible Americans who don’t have immediate access to documents like passports or birth certificates. Reasonable people can disagree about public policy.
findings.note: Campaign newsletter issued in his name (written in the third person). Describes the SAVE America Act's citizenship-document rule and the arguments on each side, then moves to the point that election officials are being pressured. Does not say whether he backs the bill.
subjects: proof of citizenship to register (SAVE America Act)

findings.passage: Accurate voter rolls matter. So does protecting every eligible citizen’s right to vote.
findings.note: Campaign newsletter issued in his name. Written after a Supreme Court order let a federal citizenship-verification database keep operating while groups say it has wrongly flagged citizens as noncitizens. Raised in the same breath: voter-roll accuracy and eligible citizens' access.

findings.passage: But do not use the power of the federal government to frighten state officials, revive debunked election narratives, or create the impression that American elections are hopelessly corrupted without producing evidence to support that claim.
findings.note: Campaign newsletter issued in his name, under the heading "Threatening Election Officials Is Not Election Security", after a federal official warned of prosecuting illegal voting and threatened state officials over voter information and the SAVE system. A short list just before it reads: "Secure voter information. Protect election workers. Maintain accurate voter rolls."

findings.passage: Doug Chapin, director of the school’s Program for Excellence in Election Administration, recommends the report “to anyone interested in going behind the partisan rhetoric and focusing instead on what it takes to move voter ID from policy to practice.”
findings.note: Minnesota Lawyer quoted him, as a University of Minnesota election-administration director, on a student report about the costs and effects of Minnesota's proposed photo voter ID constitutional amendment. The quoted part is his; the rest of the sentence is the outlet's. Old and not a campaign statement.
